name: Product Metrics
title: The metrics round, drilled: define success, diagnose the drop, defend the trade-off.
lede: A mock focused on the analytical round — 'what metrics for X', 'DAU dropped 10%, why', 'how would you measure success'. We run a realistic prompt, then I show you how to build a clean metric tree, pick a north star, reason about guardrails, and structure a diagnosis.
reassure: 100% money-back guarantee — if it isn't useful, tell me and I'll refund it in full.
forYou: Facing a metrics or analytical PM round soon
Listing random metrics instead of building a clean tree
Unsure how to reason about a north star and guardrails
Stumbling on 'a metric dropped — why' diagnosis prompts
Wanting structure for measuring feature success
notForYou: You want a product sense or strategy round (book those instead)
You need a deep SQL or data-engineering tutorial
You want written feedback, not a live mock

howItWorks.d: Checkout in your local currency and you'll be handed straight to booking.
Pick a slot and share your target role and level.
A realistic metrics prompt, timed, on Google Meet — you answer as if it's the real round.
We break down your answer and I show you how to build metric trees and structure diagnoses cleanly.

deliverables: A repeatable way to build a metric tree from any prompt
A clear approach to north-star and guardrail reasoning
A structured method for 'why did this metric move' diagnoses
Honest feedback on where your analysis got loose
The specific fixes to practice before the real round

faq.a: Whether you can define what success means for a product, choose the right metrics and guardrails, and reason clearly when a number moves — with structure, not a guessing spree.

faq.q: Do I need to be great at math?
faq.a: No. This is about structured analytical thinking, not arithmetic. We focus on how you frame and reason, which is what interviewers actually score.

faq.q: Will we cover diagnosing a metric drop?
faq.a: Yes — 'a metric dropped, why?' is one of the most common formats and we'll practice a clean, hypothesis-driven approach to it.

finalCta.title: Own the metrics round.
finalCta.sub: Book a focused mock and leave with a framework you can apply to any prompt.
